activities.name: Christ the Redeemer & Corcovado Rack Railway
activities.description: Ride the historic cog railway through the dense Atlantic Rainforest of Tijuca National Park to the summit of Corcovado, where the iconic 38-meter Christ the Redeemer statue stands with arms outstretched over the entire city. Go early morning to beat cloud cover and crowds.
activities.duration_note: Book the rack railway — avoid vans. Early morning for clearest views

activities.name: Sugarloaf Mountain Cable Car at Sunset
activities.description: Ride the two-stage cable car from Praia Vermelha up to Morro da Urca, then to the summit of Sugarloaf at golden hour — watching the sun drop behind the Tijuca mountains while the city, Guanabara Bay, and Copacabana beach glow below in warm amber light.
activities.duration_note: Aim for the last entry slot of the day for the best sunset light

activities.name: Tandem Hang Gliding from Pedra Bonita
activities.description: Sprint off a granite rainforest cliff with an instructor strapped to your back, soaring over the entire Tijuca National Park canopy and descending onto the white sands of São Conrado beach — one of the most accessible and spectacular hang gliding experiences in the world.
activities.duration_note: Mandatory tandem with licensed instructor — no solo flights

activities.name: Ilha Grande Schooner Island Cruise & Snorkel
activities.description: Board a traditional schooner or speedboat from Vila do Abraão to navigate the hidden emerald bays of Ilha Grande — one of Brazil's most pristine Atlantic island ecosystems — stopping at the luminous blue waters of Lagoa Azul and secluded beaches accessible only by sea.
activities.location: Ilha Grande, Angra dos Reis, RJ

activities.name: Paraty Colonial Walk & Gold Trail Hike
activities.description: Wander the perfectly preserved 17th-century cobblestone colonial center of Paraty — car-free streets, whitewashed facades, and colorful window frames — then hike the historic 18th-century Gold Trail into the Serra da Bocaina mountains, the route once used to transport Minas Gerais gold to the sea.

activities.name: Feijoada Completa at Casa da Feijoada
activities.description: Sit down to Brazil's most iconic meal — Feijoada Completa, a slow-cooked black bean stew layered with smoked pork ribs, sausage, and dried beef, served with farofa, braised kale, orange slices, and rice at the celebrated Casa da Feijoada in Ipanema. Traditionally eaten on Saturdays.

activities.name: Copacabana Beach Biscoito Globo & Mate Leão
activities.description: Experience Rio's most beloved beach ritual — flagging down a roving vendor for a bag of Biscoito Globo (light, airy puffed manioc starch rings) and a styrofoam cup of Mate Leão (sweetened iced black tea with lime juice squeezed fresh), eaten with your feet in the sand.

activities.name: Rio Scenarium & Arcos da Lapa Samba Night
activities.description: Spend the night in Lapa — Rio's legendary bohemian samba neighborhood — starting at Rio Scenarium, a three-floor converted antique warehouse with live samba bands and a theatrical atmosphere, then spill out to the raw Friday street party under the iconic Arcos da Lapa aqueduct arches.

activities.name: Pedra do Sal Monday Roots Samba Circle
activities.description: Every Monday evening, one of samba's most historically significant birthplaces — Pedra do Sal in the Saúde neighborhood — comes alive with an authentic, neighborhood roots samba circle completely free to attend, where musicians and locals mingle in a centuries-old call-and-response tradition.
activities.duration_note: Monday evenings only — free entry, pay for drinks

activities.name: Pelourinho Colonial Walk & Olodum Drumming
activities.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Pelourinho — Salvador's extraordinary hillside colonial center of pastel-colored baroque mansions, mosaic-tiled plazas, and the gold-encrusted São Francisco Church — capped by watching live Olodum percussion rehearsals, the legendary drum group that brought Bahian rhythms to the world stage.

activities.name: Cachoeira do Fumaça Canyon Trek
activities.description: Hike a demanding full-day mountain trail to the rim of the Fumaça Canyon — where a 340-meter waterfall vaporizes completely into mist before ever reaching the canyon floor, creating a permanent cloud below. One of the most surreal natural spectacles in Brazil.
activities.duration_note: Full day — depart early. Strong fitness required

activities.name: Pratinha Cave Underground River Tubing
activities.description: Float on inner tubes through the crystal-clear subterranean river systems of Pratinha cave — the water an impossibly vivid blue from filtered limestone light — wearing only a headlamp and life vest as the cave channels narrow around you.

activities.name: Speedboat Island Hop to Boipeba
activities.description: Launch from Morro de São Paulo by speedboat, navigating open Atlantic ocean and winding mangrove channels to the even more remote island of Boipeba — stopping at floating oyster bars anchored in the bay, with swimming stops in untouched coral reefs along the route.

activities.name: Lençóis Maranhenses Dune & Blue Lagoon Trek
activities.description: Ride a modified 4x4 truck across wild sand tracks then trek over vast, pure-white coastal dunes to discover hundreds of seasonal freshwater lagoons trapped between the crests — vivid turquoise pools surrounded by blinding white sand in one of the most otherworldly landscapes on the planet.
activities.duration_note: Seasonal: lagoons only exist May through September. Park e-ticket required in advance via ICMBio portal (~$19 USD for foreign adults)

activities.name: Acarajé from a Baiana de Acarajé
activities.description: Buy Acarajé exclusively from one of Salvador's white-dressed street-side Baianas — a deep-fried black-eyed pea fritter sizzling in pungent dendê palm oil, split open and stuffed with vatapá (creamy shrimp paste), caruru, and dried shrimp. A UNESCO-recognized street food tradition unique to Bahia.

activities.name: Moqueca Baiana Clay Pot Seafood Stew
activities.description: Sit down to Bahia's most celebrated dish — Moqueca Baiana, a rich, aromatic seafood stew of fresh fish, prawns, or crab cooked with coconut milk, dendê palm oil, cilantro, and peppers in the traditional unglazed clay pot that gives the dish its earthy, smoky depth.

activities.name: Terça da Bênção — Pelourinho Tuesday Street Party
activities.description: Every Tuesday night, the entire Pelourinho neighborhood erupts into the Terça da Bênção — a massive free open-air street party where multiple live percussion and axé music groups perform simultaneously across the colonial plazas, drawing thousands of locals and visitors into the streets.
activities.duration_note: Tuesday evenings only — free entry, pay for drinks

activities.name: Rio Vermelho Craft Beer & Caipirinha Night
activities.description: Explore Salvador's most bohemian and intellectually vibrant neighborhood — Rio Vermelho — gathering around Largo de Santana with its cluster of bars, craft beer spots, and outdoor tables where artists, musicians, and locals share caipirinhas and cold beers in a relaxed, creative atmosphere.

activities.name: Meeting of the Waters Boat Expedition
activities.description: Witness one of the world's most extraordinary natural phenomena — the dark, tea-colored Rio Negro and the pale sandy Rio Solimões flowing side-by-side for over 6 kilometers without mixing, their waters kept separate by differences in temperature, speed, and density in a perfectly straight boundary line.

activities.name: Nocturnal Caiman Spotting & Piranha Fishing
activities.description: Navigate the flooded igapó forest channels by motorized canoe after dark, using high-powered spotlights to find the red eye-glow of black caimans lurking in the jungle water, then fish for piranhas using raw meat on simple hand lines in one of the most thrillingly atmospheric experiences the Amazon offers.
activities.duration_note: Best during high water season May–August when forests are flooded

activities.name: Multi-Day Deep Jungle Survival Trek
activities.description: Strip down to basic gear and hike deep into primary Amazon rainforest with a native Amazonian guide — learning to build palm-leaf shelters, identify medicinal plants, track wildlife, and forage for food in the world's most biodiverse terrestrial ecosystem. A genuinely transformative wilderness experience.
activities.duration_note: 3 days / 2 nights. Yellow fever vaccination required. Heavy DEET essential

activities.name: Pink River Dolphin Interaction
activities.description: Enter the warm tea-colored waters of the Rio Negro alongside IBAMA-licensed guides to interact with wild boto — the legendary pink river dolphins of the Amazon, the largest river dolphins in the world, curious and surprisingly gentle in their encounters with swimmers.
activities.duration_note: Licensed IBAMA guides required — only at authorized interaction sites

activities.name: Tacacá Soup & Tambaqui Ribs at Mercado Adolpho Lisboa
activities.description: Visit the magnificent Art Nouveau wrought-iron Mercado Adolpho Lisboa on the riverfront for the definitive Amazon food experience — tongue-numbing Tacacá soup made from yellow tucupi manioc broth and jambu greens, followed by massive Tambaqui river fish ribs grilled over open coals.

activities.name: Largo de São Sebastião Street Performers & Forró
activities.description: Gather in the lively plaza directly in front of Manaus' iconic pink Teatro Amazonas opera house — filling nightly with outdoor beer tables, street performers, and regional musicians playing Carimbó and Forró rhythms unique to the Amazon basin in a beautiful colonial setting.

activities.name: Jaguar Boat Safari along Rio Cuiabá
activities.description: Navigate the river convergence zones deep in the northern Pantanal at the height of dry season — scanning the banks where jaguars, the largest cats in the Americas, descend to hunt caiman in the shallows. The Pantanal offers the highest jaguar encounter probability on Earth during this season.
activities.duration_note: Seasonal: July through October (dry season) only. High-clearance 4x4 or lodge transfer required from Cuiabá via Transpantaneira

activities.name: Olho d'Água Crystal River Float
activities.description: Float down a limestone-filtered river with near-100% visibility — the water so pure you can see every grain of sand on the riverbed and every scale on the massive Piraputanga fish schooling around you. One of the clearest natural river environments anywhere in the world.

activities.name: Anhumas Abyss Spelunking & Abseil
activities.description: Descend 72 meters through a narrow cave crack by abseil into a cathedral-like underground cavern — emerging inside a vast interior space housing a crystal-clear underground lake surrounded by towering stalagmites and stalactites. One of Brazil's most technically spectacular adventure experiences.
activities.duration_note: Limited daily slots — book well in advance. Physical fitness required for abseil

activities.name: Caldo de Piranha & Pintado ao Urucum
activities.description: Try the Pantanal's two legendary dishes — Caldo de Piranha, a thick, intensely seasoned soup made from blended piranhas traditionally consumed as a local energy booster, followed by Pintado ao Urucum, a massive local catfish prepared with native urucum seed paste, coconut milk, and melted cheese.

activities.name: Taboa Bar — Herb-Infused Cachaça Tasting
activities.description: Settle in at Bonito's most beloved local bar — Taboa Bar on Rua Coronel Pilad Rebuá — for flights of house-distilled cachaça infused with local Cerrado herbs, cinnamon bark, and native fruits. A warm, sociable spot where Pantanal guides and eco-tourists swap stories over artisanal cane spirit.

activities.name: Macuco Safari Powerboat Ride Under the Falls
activities.description: Ride a twin-engine inflatable powerboat up the Iguazu River canyon at full throttle, plunging directly into the thundering wall of spray and mist at the base of the falls — one of the most viscerally intense adventure experiences in South America. You will be completely soaked.
activities.duration_note: Waterproof your phone and belongings — you will get completely drenched

activities.name: Garganta do Diabo Boardwalk — Devil's Throat
activities.description: Walk the metal boardwalks suspended directly over the Iguazu River to the edge of the Garganta do Diabo — the Devil's Throat, the most powerful section of the falls — where 700,000 liters of water per second plunge into a roaring abyss of permanent white mist and rainbow arcs.
activities.duration_note: Bring waterproof cases — spray reaches the walkway. Go early for lighter crowds

activities.name: Canyon Itaimbezinho Hiking Expedition
activities.description: Hike along the rim and into the gorge of one of Brazil's most dramatic structural canyon rifts — sheer 600-meter basalt walls dropping into a narrow canyon floor draped in native Araucaria pine trees, with the roar of twin waterfalls echoing up from below.
activities.location: Aparados da Serra National Park, RS
activities.duration_note: Pack thermals June–August — temperatures can drop near freezing in the southern highlands

activities.name: Churrasco Gaúcho & Chimarrão
activities.description: Experience the definitive Southern Brazilian food ritual — Churrasco Gaúcho, massive cuts of beef, lamb, and pork roasted over open hardwood fire pits seasoned only with coarse rock salt, followed by Chimarrão, the bitter hot yerba mate loose tea shared communally in a gourd with a silver bombilla straw.
activities.location: Foz do Iguaçu / Rio Grande do Sul

activities.name: Avenida Jorge Schimmelpfeng Triple-Border Bar Night
activities.description: Explore the lively open-air bar strip of Foz do Iguaçu — a city uniquely positioned on the triple border of Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay — with brewpubs, ice bars, and open-air folklore shows, or cross the Tancredo Neves Bridge to drink Malbec and eat Argentine steak in Puerto Iguazú.
activities.duration_note: If crossing to Argentina — must clear official immigration at the bridge checkpoint
